require 'net/http'
require 'openssl'
require 'json'
require 'connection_pool'
require 'digest'
require 'securerandom'

module RemoteAdmin
  class CredentialStore
    attr_reader :credentials

    def initialize
      @credentials = {}
      @mutex = Mutex.new
    end

    def store(host, username, auth_token, nonce)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @credentials[host] = {
          username: username,
          auth_token: auth_token,
          nonce: nonce,
          stored_at: Time.now.to_i
        }
      end
    end

    def retrieve(host)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @credentials[host]
      end
    end

    def clear(host)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @credentials.delete(host)
      end
    end
  end

  class AuthenticationHandler
    NONCE_TTL = 300
    PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 210_000
    KEY_LENGTH = 32

    def initialize(credential_store)
      @credential_store = credential_store
    end

    def authenticate(host, username, password)
      nonce = request_nonce(host)
      auth_token = compute_auth_token(username, password, nonce)
      @credential_store.store(host, username, auth_token, nonce)
      auth_token
    end

    def reauthenticate(host, password)
      cred = @credential_store.retrieve(host)
      return nil unless cred
      # Request fresh nonce and recompute token from password
      nonce = request_nonce(host)
      auth_token = compute_auth_token(cred[:username], password, nonce)
      @credential_store.store(host, cred[:username], auth_token, nonce)
      auth_token
    end

    private

    def request_nonce(host)
      # In production, this would be an HTTP call to get server nonce
      SecureRandom.hex(16)
    end

    def compute_auth_token(username, password, nonce)
      # Derive key material from the password using a proper KDF (PBKDF2)
      # instead of a single unsalted SHA-256 pass. The nonce is used as the
      # salt so each token is bound to a fresh challenge.
      salt = Digest::SHA256.digest("#{username}:#{nonce}")
      key_material = OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(
        password,
        salt,
        PBKDF2_ITERATIONS,
        KEY_LENGTH,
        OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new
      )
      data = "#{username}:#{nonce}"
      OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', key_material, data)
    end
  end

  class ConnectionManager
    MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5
    POOL_TIMEOUT = 10

    def initialize(auth_handler, credential_store)
      @auth_handler = auth_handler
      @credential_store = credential_store
      @pools = {}
      @pool_mutex = Mutex.new
    end

    def get_connection(host, port = 443)
      pool = get_or_create_pool(host, port)
      pool.with do |conn|
        ensure_authenticated(conn, host)
        conn
      end
    end

    def execute_command(host, command, port = 443)
      pool = get_or_create_pool(host, port)
      pool.with do |conn|
        ensure_authenticated(conn, host)
        send_authenticated_request(conn, host, command)
      end
    end

    private

    def get_or_create_pool(host, port)
      @pool_mutex.synchronize do
        key = "#{host}:#{port}"
        @pools[key] ||= ConnectionPool.new(size: MAX_POOL_SIZE, timeout: POOL_TIMEOUT) do
          create_connection(host, port)
        end
      end
    end

    def create_connection(host, port)
      http = Net::HTTP.new(host, port)
      http.use_ssl = true
      http.verify_mode = OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_PEER
      http.open_timeout = 5
      http.read_timeout = 10
      http
    end

    def ensure_authenticated(conn, host)
      cred = @credential_store.retrieve(host)
      return unless cred
      conn.instance_variable_set(:@auth_token, cred[:auth_token])
    end

    def send_authenticated_request(conn, host, command)
      token = conn.instance_variable_get(:@auth_token)
      return { error: 'Not authenticated' } unless token

      request = Net::HTTP::Post.new('/api/v1/execute')
      request['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
      request['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{token}"
      request.body = JSON.generate({ command: command })

      response = conn.request(request)
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    end
  end

  class SessionSerializer
    SERIALIZATION_VERSION = 1

    def self.save_session(credential_store, filepath)
      # Only save metadata, never persist auth tokens
      data = {
        version: SERIALIZATION_VERSION,
        timestamp: Time.now.to_i,
        sessions: credential_store.credentials.transform_values do |cred|
          {
            username: cred[:username],
            stored_at: cred[:stored_at]
          }
        end
      }
      File.write(filepath, JSON.generate(data), mode: 'w', perm: 0600)
    end

    def self.load_session(credential_store, filepath)
      return false unless File.exist?(filepath)
      raw = File.read(filepath)
      data = JSON.parse(raw, symbolize_names: true)
      return false unless data[:version] == SERIALIZATION_VERSION

      # Only restore host/username mapping, not tokens
      data[:sessions].each do |host, cred|
        credential_store.store(
          host.to_s,
          cred[:username],
          nil,
          nil
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  class CLI
    SESSION_FILE = File.join(Dir.home, '.remote_admin_session')

    def initialize
      @credential_store = CredentialStore.new
      @auth_handler = AuthenticationHandler.new(@credential_store)
      @connection_manager = ConnectionManager.new(@auth_handler, @credential_store)
      load_saved_session
    end

    def connect(host, username, password)
      @auth_handler.authenticate(host, username, password)
      save_session
      puts "Connected to #{host} as #{username}"
    end

    def reconnect(host, password)
      token = @auth_handler.reauthenticate(host, password)
      if token
        save_session
        puts "Reconnected to #{host} with fresh authentication"
      else
        puts "No cached session for #{host}"
      end
    end

    def run(host, command)
      result = @connection_manager.execute_command(host, command)
      puts result.to_json
    end

    def disconnect(host)
      @credential_store.clear(host)
      save_session
      puts "Disconnected from #{host}"
    end

    private

    def save_session
      SessionSerializer.save_session(@credential_store, SESSION_FILE)
    end

    def load_saved_session
      SessionSerializer.load_session(@credential_store, SESSION_FILE)
    end
  end
end

# Entry point
if __FILE__ == $0
  cli = RemoteAdmin::CLI.new
  case ARGV[0]
  when 'connect'
    cli.connect(ARGV[1], ARGV[2], ARGV[3])
  when 'reconnect'
    cli.reconnect(ARGV[1], ARGV[2])
  when 'run'
    cli.run(ARGV[1], ARGV[2])
  when 'disconnect'
    cli.disconnect(ARGV[1])
  else
    puts "Usage: remote_admin {connect|reconnect|run|disconnect} [args...]"
  end
end
